mainTopic: The prophetesses אביגיל, חולדה, and אסתר: proofs of their prophecy, why חולדה prophesied in ירמיה's time, the return of the ten tribes, and חולדה's character and family line
overview: This amud continues the גמרא's list of the seven prophetesses. It first finishes the story of אביגיל. דוד thanks her for keeping him from דמים ('bloods'), and the plural hints that she saved him from two sins. Her word זאת also hints that דוד would later stumble with בת שבע, which shows she had prophecy. רב נחמן compares her quiet request that דוד 'remember' her to two folk sayings. Next comes חולדה, and the גמרא asks how she could prophesy when ירמיה was alive. One answer is that she was his relative and the king hoped women are more compassionate. רבי יוחנן answers instead that ירמיה was away bringing back the ten tribes, who then lived under יאשיהו. אסתר is proven a prophetess because she 'put on מלכות', meaning רוח הקדש. Finally, רב נחמן says pride does not suit women, as seen in דבורה and חולדה. He also teaches that חולדה descends from both יהושע and רחב, who converted and married him and had daughters.

steps.title: דוד claims נבל is a rebel against the king
steps.stepSummary: דוד answers אביגיל: נבל is a מורד במלכות, so no trial is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is a rebel against the kingship, and there is no need to judge him.
steps.whatsHappening: דוד is answering אביגיל's objection, which began on the previous amud, that he cannot judge נבל without a proper trial. He says a rebel against the king does not get the usual court process.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד had already been anointed by שמואל, and נבל refused his request. דוד therefore treats נבל's refusal as rebellion against the crown, and the normal rules of a trial do not apply to that category.

keyTerms.meaning: To judge him (in a normal trial)

phrases.english: He is a rebel against the kingship,
and there is no need to try him in court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the dialogue earlier, answering אביגיל's procedural objection.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מורד במלכות may be punished without a regular trial.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rebel against the king is not given ordinary court procedure.

steps.title: אביגיל answers that שאול is still king
steps.stepSummary: אביגיל rejects דוד's claim, because שאול still reigns and דוד's kingship is not yet public.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: שאול is still alive, and your coin has not yet gone out into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: אביגיל pushes back on דוד's argument. As long as שאול is alive and ruling, דוד cannot act with royal power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about a מורד במלכות only applies to a king who is actually ruling. דוד was anointed, but his 'coin' (his public authority) is not yet in use. So there is no 'kingship' that נבל could have rebelled against yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Your coin or seal, a symbol of royal authority

phrases.english: She said to him: Saul is still alive
and your coin has not yet gone out into the world.
phrases.notes: Your kingship isn't official in public yet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects דוד's claim from step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole claim that נבל can be treated as a מורד במלכות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: דוד's royal authority is not yet active while שאול reigns.

steps.title: דוד accepts and blesses אביגיל
steps.stepSummary: דוד agrees with אביגיל and blesses her for keeping him from דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: 'Blessed is your good sense, and blessed are you, who kept me this day from coming into bloodshed.'
steps.whatsHappening: דוד concedes the argument and thanks אביגיל by quoting the פסוק in שמואל א. This ends the legal debate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד admits he was about to make a terrible mistake. The plural word דמים in his words becomes the launching point for the גמרא's next question.

keyTerms.meaning: You held me back, you prevented me

steps.whatToRemember: דוד accepted אביגיל's argument that he had no royal power to kill נבל while שאול was king.

phrases.english: He said to her: 'Blessed is your good sense'
and blessed are you, who held me back
this day from coming into bloodshed.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: דוד accepts the rejection in step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: דוד concedes and thanks אביגיל for stopping him.

steps.title: Why the plural word for blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that דמים is plural and implies two things.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Bloods' means two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא zooms in on one word in the פסוק. It is setting up the next step, which will explain what the 'second blood' was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one kind of blood is visible so far: killing נבל. If that were all, the פסוק should have used the singular דם. The plural form demands a second sin that was avoided.

phrases.english: 'Bloods' implies two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes a word from the פסוק quoted in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plural word דמים in דוד's blessing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only one bloodshed (killing נבל) has been mentioned, so the plural seems unexplained.

steps.title: The second danger was desire for אביגיל
steps.stepSummary: The second 'blood' refers to דוד's desire for אביגיל, which he asked her to act on.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this teaches that she uncovered her leg, and he went three parasangs by its light. He said to her: Listen to me!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about the plural. The second 'blood' was a near sin of intimacy with אביגיל, who was a married woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sins were prevented that day: killing נבל, and a forbidden relationship with אביגיל. The 'blood' in the second case refers to forbidden intimacy (often understood as נדה blood). דוד was so taken by her that he traveled three פרסאות by the 'light' of her.
steps.confusionAlert: Both 'bloods' are dangers that were avoided. Neither one actually happened, which is why דוד blesses her.

phrases.english: Rather, it teaches that she uncovered her leg
phrases.notes: The 'light' in the next phrase is a way of describing the attraction her uncovered leg stirred up.

phrases.english: and he walked by its light for three parasangs,
he said to her: Listen to me!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the second event hinted at by the plural word.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דמים refers only to killing נבל.
steps.terutzMaskana: דמים covers both killing נבל and a forbidden relationship with אביגיל.

steps.title: אביגיל refuses דוד
steps.stepSummary: אביגיל refuses by quoting her words: 'Let this not be a stumbling block for you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: 'Let this not be a stumbling block for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביגיל turns דוד down using a פסוק from her own speech. This step sets up the next move, where the גמרא will read meaning into the word זאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her words in the פסוק are read here as a refusal: do not let this act trip you up. This keeps דוד from the second 'blood.'

phrases.english: She said to him: 'Let this not be'
a stumbling block for you.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה לוֹ: לֹא תִהְיֶה זֹאת לְךָ לְפוּקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביגיל's response to דוד's request in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביגיל refused דוד, citing the danger of stumbling.

steps.title: The word 'this' hints at בת שבע
steps.stepSummary: From the word זאת, the גמרא infers that another stumbling block would come: the incident of בת שבע.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This' implies that there is another one. And what is it? The incident of בת שבע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads closely: 'THIS should not trip you' suggests that something ELSE will. It identifies that 'something else' as בת שבע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זאת limits her warning to the present case. By implication (מכלל), there is a different future case where דוד would stumble. אביגיל was hinting at a future event.

phrases.english: 'This' implies that there is another one,
and what is it? The incident of Bathsheba.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of step 6.
steps.raayaObject: אביגיל foresaw a future stumbling block.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The limiting word זאת in שמואל א כה:לא.

steps.title: It happened just as she said
steps.stepSummary: In the end, the incident with בת שבע did happen, confirming her hint.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the end, that is how it was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this section by noting that her hint came true. This shows that אביגיל had prophecy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the point of the whole section in the sugya about the נביאות, the prophetesses. Her accurate prediction about בת שבע proves she was a prophetess.
steps.whatToRemember: The plural דמים points to two avoided sins: killing נבל, and a forbidden relationship with אביגיל. Her word זאת hinted at בת שבע, which proves she was a prophetess.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the proof that אביגיל belongs on the list of the seven prophetesses that the גמרא is discussing.

phrases.english: And in the end, that is how it was.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the inference of step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביגיל's hint came true, which shows her prophecy.

steps.title: אביגיל asks דוד to remember her
steps.stepSummary: While blessing דוד and parting from him, אביגיל asked him to 'remember your maidservant.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bond of life.' When she was taking leave of him, she said to him: 'When God does good for my lord, remember your maidservant.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another detail from the story. On her way out, אביגיל asks דוד to remember her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She came to save her husband, yet she hints that if נבל dies, דוד should think of her. This sets up רב נחמן's comment in the next step. Later, after נבל died, דוד did marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: Bound in the bond of life

phrases.english: 'And the soul of my lord shall be'
bound in the bond of life,'

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲווֹת מִיפַּטְרָא מִינֵּיהּ אָמְרָה לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: when she was parting from him she said to him:
'And when God does good for my lord,'
you shall remember your maidservant.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲווֹת מִיפַּטְרָא מִינֵּיהּ אָמְרָה לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new observation about אביגיל's words, building on the same story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביגיל hinted that דוד should remember her in the future.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the woman with the spindle
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן applies a folk saying: while a woman talks, she is already holding her spindle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: This is what people say: A woman, while chatting, holds her spindle.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains אביגיל's behavior with a popular proverb about doing two things at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While talking about one matter (saving נבל), she was already working on another (her own future with דוד). The spindle stands for productive work done quietly during conversation.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (a folk saying)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said,
this is what people say:
A woman, while chatting, holds the spindle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on אביגיל's request in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביגיל pursued a second goal while handling the first.

steps.title: Another version: the stooping goose
steps.stepSummary: Another version of רב נחמן's saying: the goose walks with its head bent, but its eyes look far ahead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: The goose walks along bent over, but its eyes look far ahead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the proverb רב נחמן quoted. The point is the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goose looks humble and focused on the ground, yet it is scanning for what it wants. In the same way, אביגיל acted humbly and pleaded for her husband while keeping her eye on her future.

keyTerms.meaning: Look far ahead, peer into the distance

steps.whatToRemember: Both proverbs make the same point: אביגיל, while pleading to save נבל, also quietly prepared for her future with דוד.

phrases.english: Some say:
The goose walks along stooping,
but its eyes look far ahead.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי שָׁפֵיל וְאָזֵיל בַּר אֲווֹזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternate version of the proverb in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A humble outward stance can hide a far-sighted aim.

steps.title: חולדה is listed as a prophetess
steps.stepSummary: חולדה is named as one of the prophetesses, based on the פסוק where יאשיהו's messengers go to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: חולדה was a prophetess, as it is written: 'So חלקיהו the כהן, and אחיקם, and עכבור, etc. went' to חולדה the prophetess.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds חולדה to its list of prophetesses and brings a פסוק to show she was one. This also sets up the next question about ירמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows that King יאשיהו sent important officials to ask חולדה for a prophecy. That shows she was a recognized נביאה. The 'וגו׳' (etc.) points to the end of the פסוק, which calls her 'חולדה הנביאה'.

keyTerms.meaning: חולדה, a prophetess in the time of King יאשיהו
חלקיהו הכהן, one of the king's messengers
'etc.', meaning the rest of the פסוק continues

phrases.english: Huldah, as it is written:
"So Hilkiah the priest went,
and Ahikam and Achbor, etc."
phrases.notes: The rest of the פסוק (מלכים ב כב:יד) says they went 'to חולדה הנביאה'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of the seven prophetesses after אביגיל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חולדה was a prophetess, as shown by the king's messengers going to her.

steps.title: How could חולדה prophesy where ירמיה was present?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: ירמיה was the greater נביא of that generation, so how could חולדה prophesy in his presence?
steps.simpleTranslation: But in a place where ירמיה was found, how could she prophesy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a difficulty with the story it just quoted. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירמיה lived at the same time and was the greater נביא. Out of respect, a lesser נביא should not speak prophecy in front of a greater one. So it looks wrong that חולדה gave the prophecy.

keyTerms.meaning: ירמיה, the leading נביא of that time

phrases.english: But in a place where Jeremiah was present,
how could she prophesy?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְמָקוֹם דְּקָאֵי יִרְמְיָה הֵיכִי מִתְנַבְּיָא אִיהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that חולדה prophesied in ירמיה's generation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Out of respect, a lesser נביא should not prophesy in the presence of a greater one.

steps.title: חולדה was ירמיה's relative, so he did not mind
steps.stepSummary: The school of רב answers that חולדה was related to ירמיה, so he was not bothered by her prophesying.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רב said in the name of רב: חולדה was a relative of ירמיה, and he did not object to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. ירמיה was family to חולדה, so he did not take it as disrespect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was respect toward ירמיה. If ירמיה himself was not bothered, because she was his relative, there is no disrespect. The rule about respect is not cancelled. Here the person being respected simply did not mind.

phrases.english: The school of Rav say in the name of Rav:
Huldah was a relative of Jeremiah,
and he did not object to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual circumstance: a family relationship removes the concern
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חולדה was showing disrespect by prophesying where ירמיה was present.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because she was his relative, ירמיה did not object, so there was no disrespect.

steps.title: Why would יאשיהו skip ירמיה and send to חולדה?
steps.stepSummary: Even if ירמיה did not mind, why did King יאשיהו choose חולדה over the greater נביא?
steps.simpleTranslation: But יאשיהו himself, how could he leave ירמיה aside and send to her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second question, this time about the king's choice. It is setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer explained why ירמיה did not object. It did not explain why the king would go to the lesser נביא in the first place. That is the new problem here.

keyTerms.meaning: יאשיהו, the righteous king of יהודה

phrases.english: And Josiah himself, how could he leave Jeremiah aside
and send to her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer in step 14 but raises a new difficulty from the king's side.
steps.kashyaTarget: יאשיהו's decision to send messengers to חולדה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A king seeking prophecy should go to the greatest נביא available, which was ירמיה.

steps.title: Women are more compassionate
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי שילא answers that יאשיהו went to חולדה because women are more compassionate. He hoped she would pray for mercy or soften the message.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי שילא said: because women are compassionate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why the king chose חולדה. He hoped a woman would be more merciful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יאשיהו had just found the ספר תורה and feared a harsh punishment. He went to חולדה hoping her compassion would bring a gentler response. In this answer ירמיה was available, but the king chose on purpose.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Sheila say:
Because women are compassionate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the motive behind the choice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Going to חולדה instead of ירמיה makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: יאשיהו chose חולדה deliberately, hoping for a more merciful response.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: ירמיה was away bringing back the ten tribes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer to both questions: ירמיה was not there at all, because he had gone to bring back the עשרת השבטים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: ירמיה was not there, because he had gone to bring back the ten tribes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן offers another way to answer both questions. ירמיה simply was not around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers assumed ירמיה was present and explained why that was not a problem. רבי יוחנן removes the problem completely: ירמיה was away. That claim, that the ten tribes were brought back, now needs proof.

keyTerms.meaning: the ten tribes exiled by אשור

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not adding to the earlier answers. He is giving a separate approach in which there was never a problem, since ירמיה was not present.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Jeremiah was not there,
because he went to bring back the ten tribes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: יִרְמְיָה לָא הֲוָה הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative answer to the questions in steps 13 and 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual: denies the assumption behind the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ירמיה was present when חולדה prophesied.
steps.terutzMaskana: ירמיה was away bringing back the ten tribes, so there was no conflict.

steps.title: How do we know ירמיה brought them back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that ירמיה actually brought back the ten tribes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that he brought them back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof of רבי יוחנן's claim. This sets up the proof that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ten tribes were exiled long before ירמיה. Saying they returned is a big historical claim, so the גמרא wants a source in the פסוקים.

phrases.english: And from where do we derive that he brought them back?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי יוחנן's claim in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that the ten tribes returned in ירמיה's time

steps.title: Proof from the prophecy that יובל will end
steps.stepSummary: יחזקאל prophesied that יובל would stop in the future. That means it was still in force then. יובל only applies when all the tribes are in the land, so the tribes must have returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'For the seller shall not return to what he sold.' Is it possible that יובל had already stopped, and a נביא prophesies that it will stop? Rather, this teaches that ירמיה brought them back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that the tribes returned, using a prophecy of יחזקאל about יובל ending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יובל only works when all the tribes live in ארץ ישראל. If the ten tribes were still in exile, יובל would already be over, and there would be no reason to prophesy that it 'will' stop. So יובל must have been back in force, which means ירמיה had brought the tribes back.

keyTerms.meaning: the Jubilee year, when sold land returns to its owner
the seller to what he sold

steps.confusionAlert: The key fact behind the proof is not written here: יובל applies only when all the tribes are settled in the land. Without that fact the proof is hard to follow.

phrases.english: As it is written: "For the seller
shall not return to that which he has sold"
phrases.notes: יחזקאל ז:יג, meaning that יובל will stop.

phrases.english: Is it possible that the Jubilee had already ceased,
and a prophet prophesies about it that it will cease?
Rather, this teaches that Jeremiah brought them back,

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״כִּי הַמּוֹכֵר אֶל הַמִּמְכָּר לֹא יָשׁוּב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 18 with a proof from a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That ירמיה brought back the ten tribes
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל ז:יג, together with the rule that יובל requires all the tribes in the land
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that, according to רבי יוחנן, יובל was briefly back in force near the end of the first בית המקדש period.

steps.title: יאשיהו ruled over the returned tribes
steps.stepSummary: The returned tribes were ruled by יאשיהו. Proof: the פסוק links him to the altar in בית אל, which was in the land of the ten tribes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And יאשיהו son of אמון ruled over them, as it is written: 'He said, What is this marker I see? The men of the city told him: It is the grave of the man of God who came from יהודה and proclaimed these things that you did against the altar in בית אל.' What did יאשיהו have to do with the altar in בית אל? Rather, this teaches that יאשיהו ruled over them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רבי יוחנן's statement: the returning tribes came under יאשיהו's rule. It brings a פסוק to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית אל was in the kingdom of the ten tribes, not in יהודה. A king of יהודה would have no authority to act there. Since יאשיהו destroyed that altar, he must have ruled over the ten tribes.

keyTerms.meaning: יאשיהו בן אמון, king of יהודה
בית אל, a city in the kingdom of the ten tribes

phrases.english: and Josiah son of Amon ruled over them,
as it is written: "Then he said: What is that monument
which I see?
And the men of the city told him:

phrases.aramaic: הַקֶּבֶר אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר בָּא מִיהוּדָה
phrases.english: It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah
and proclaimed these things

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתָ עַל הַמִּזְבַּח בְּבֵית אֵל״,
phrases.english: that you have done against the altar in Bethel"
Now what connection did Josiah have
with the altar in Bethel?
Rather, this teaches that Josiah ruled over them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֹאשִׁיָּהוּ בֶּן אָמוֹן מָלַךְ עֲלֵיהֶן, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוחנן's line, adding that the returned tribes were under יאשיהו, with proof.
steps.raayaObject: That יאשיהו ruled over the returned ten tribes
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב כג:יז: יאשיהו acted against the altar in בית אל

steps.title: רב נחמן's proof from הושע
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן brings a different פסוק as proof that the tribes returned: 'Also יהודה, a harvest is set for you, when I return the captivity of My people.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: the proof is from here: 'Also, יהודה, a harvest is appointed for you, when I return the captivity of My people.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives another source for the return of the tribes, from a פסוק in הושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הושע prophesied to the ten tribes about returning their captivity, and connects it to יהודה. רב נחמן reads this as the return of the exiled tribes to their places. He offers it as a different source for the same claim that step 19 proved from יחזקאל and the laws of יובל.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain why חולדה prophesied instead of ירמיה. (1) ירמיה was present: he did not mind because she was his relative, and יאשיהו went to her because women are more compassionate. (2) According to רבי יוחנן, ירמיה was away bringing back the ten tribes, who then lived under יאשיהו's rule.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: from here:
"Also, O Judah, there is a harvest appointed for you,
when I return the captivity of My people."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative source for the same claim proven in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That the exiled ten tribes returned

steps.title: אסתר was a prophetess: the verse about her clothing herself in royalty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reaches אסתר, the last prophetess on its list, and quotes the פסוק it will use as proof: 'ותלבש אסתר מלכות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אסתר: as it is written, 'And it came to pass on the third day that אסתר clothed herself in royalty.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its list of seven prophetesses and starts proving that אסתר was one of them. It quotes the פסוק, but the proof is not finished yet. This step sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on an odd word in the פסוק. It says she put on 'מלכות' (royalty), not 'royal clothing'. The next steps will point out this oddness and explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: Esther, the queen from מגילת אסתר, counted here as one of the seven prophetesses
And she clothed herself / put on

phrases.english: Esther — as it is written:
phrases.notes: This continues the list of seven prophetesses from earlier in the סוגיא.

phrases.english: 'And it came to pass on the third day'
phrases.notes: אסתר ה:א, the third day of the fast, when אסתר went to the king.

phrases.english: that Esther clothed herself in royalty'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about ירמיה and the ten tribes and goes back to the list of prophetesses.

steps.title: The verse should have said royal garments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the פסוק's wording is strange: a person puts on royal clothes, not 'royalty'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It should have said 'royal garments'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem in the wording of the פסוק. It should have said 'royal garments', so why does it just say 'royalty'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: You cannot physically put on 'royalty'. You can only put on clothing. Because the wording seems wrong, the גמרא concludes that it must hint at something deeper, and that hint becomes the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: It should have said (literally, 'it needed to')

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on any opinion. It is a question about the wording of the פסוק, and answering it is what produces the proof that אסתר was a prophetess.

phrases.english: It should have said 'royal garments'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the פסוק just quoted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Clothing, not 'royalty', is what a person puts on, so the plain wording seems to be missing a word.

steps.title: She was clothed with רוח הקדש, like עמשי
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק means that רוח הקדש 'clothed' אסתר. The same verb is used for עמשי, who was clothed by a spirit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means that a holy spirit clothed her. It is written here 'and she clothed herself', and it is written there 'and a spirit clothed עמשי'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'clothed in מלכות' really means clothed in רוח הקדש. It proves this by matching the same verb in another פסוק, where a spirit 'clothed' עמשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere the word 'לבש' describes a spirit coming over a person (עמשי). So here too it means a spirit came over אסתר. Having רוח הקדש is what makes her a prophetess.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is written here... and it is written there': a formula that compares the same word in two verses
עמשי, a leader in דוד's time who was seized by a spirit (דברי הימים א יב:יט)

steps.whatToRemember: אסתר is proven to be a prophetess because 'she put on מלכות' means a holy spirit 'clothed' her, just as a spirit 'clothed' עמשי.

phrases.english: Rather, it means that a holy spirit clothed her,
it is written here: 'and she clothed herself',
and it is written there:
'And a spirit clothed Amasai, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording problem, and the answer completes the proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the word through a word-comparison with another פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק is simply describing royal clothing, with a word missing.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Clothed in מלכות' means clothed in רוח הקדש, which makes אסתר a prophetess.

steps.title: רב נחמן: haughtiness does not suit women
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says haughtiness is not fitting for women. He points to two haughty women whose names are names of unpleasant creatures: 'hornet' (דבורה) and 'weasel/marten' (חולדה).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Haughtiness is not fitting for women. There were two haughty women, and their names were ugly: one was named 'hornet' and one was named 'marten'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן makes a new statement about two of the prophetesses. He says they were haughty and that their names were unflattering, as a lesson that pride does not suit women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דבורה means a bee or hornet, and חולדה means a weasel or marten. רב נחמן reads these names as a hint that something unpleasant was connected to them, namely haughtiness. The next two steps show where the haughtiness appears in the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: Is not fitting / does not suit

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Haughtiness is not fitting for women.
There were two haughty women,
and their names were ugly:
one was named 'hornet',
and one was named 'marten'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: לָא יָאָה יְהִירוּתָא לִנְשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the list of prophetesses, the גמרא adds a separate teaching about two of them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Haughtiness does not suit women, as seen from דבורה and חולדה.

steps.title: דבורה's haughtiness: she summoned ברק
steps.stepSummary: דבורה sent for ברק to come to her instead of going to him herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the 'hornet' it is written: 'And she sent and called ברק', whereas she herself did not go to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן shows where דבורה acted haughtily. She called ברק to come to her rather than going to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the details of the פסוק (שופטים ד:ו). דבורה sent a messenger and made ברק come to her, which רב נחמן sees as a sign of pride.

keyTerms.meaning: ברק, the general who fought סיסרא
She did not go to him

phrases.english: About the 'hornet' it is written:
'And she sent and called Barak',
whereas she herself did not go to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן's claim in the case of דבורה.

steps.title: חולדה's haughtiness: 'tell the man', not 'tell the king'
steps.stepSummary: חולדה referred to King יאשיהו as 'the man' instead of 'the king'.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the 'marten' it is written: 'Say to the man', and she did not say 'Say to the king'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן shows where חולדה acted haughtily. When the king's messengers came to her, she called the king 'the man' instead of 'the king'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מלכים ב כב:טו, חולדה says 'tell the man who sent you to me'. Calling the king 'the man' rather than using his royal title is the sign of pride. This finishes רב נחמן's proof.
steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן: דבורה summoned ברק instead of going to him, and חולדה called the king 'the man'. Both are signs of haughtiness, which he says does not suit women.

phrases.english: About the 'marten' it is written:
'Say to the man',
phrases.notes: מלכים ב כב:טו, said to King יאשיהו's messengers.

phrases.english: and she did not say 'Say to the king'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second proof, this time for חולדה.

steps.title: רב נחמן: חולדה descended from יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן teaches that חולדה was a descendant of יהושע. He bases this on the similar words 'חרחס' (in her family line) and 'תמנת חרס' (where יהושע was buried).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: חולדה was one of the descendants of יהושע. It is written here 'son of חרחס', and it is written there 'in תמנת חרס'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן makes another statement about חולדה: she came from the family of יהושע. He proves it by matching a name in her family line to the name of יהושע's burial place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her family line includes 'בן חרחס', and יהושע was buried in 'תמנת חרס'. The shared sound 'חרס' links her family to יהושע. This becomes the target of the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: חולדה הנביאה, in the time of King יאשיהו
From the descendants of (literally, 'from his children's children')
חרחס, an ancestor in חולדה's family line
תמנת חרס, the place where יהושע was buried

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:

phrases.aramaic: חוּלְדָּה מִבְּנֵי בָנָיו שֶׁל יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָיְתָה —
phrases.english: Chuldah was one of the descendants of Yehoshua —
it is written here: 'son of Charchas',
phrases.notes: מלכים ב כב:יד, in the family line of חולדה's husband שלום.

phrases.english: and it is written there: 'in Timnas-Cheres'.
phrases.notes: שופטים ב:ט, where יהושע was buried.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: חוּלְדָּה מִבְּנֵי בָנָיו שֶׁל יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate teaching of רב נחמן about חולדה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חולדה descended from יהושע, shown by the word-link חרחס / תמנת חרס.

steps.title: רב עינא סבא objects: a ברייתא says חולדה descended from רחב
steps.stepSummary: רב עינא סבא quotes a ברייתא that lists eight prophets who were כהנים and descended from רחב הזונה. In that ברייתא, רבי יהודה adds that חולדה also descended from רחב, which seems to contradict רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עינא סבא challenged רב נחמן: Eight נביאים who were also כהנים came from רחב הזונה: נריה, ברוך, שריה, מחסיה, ירמיה, חלקיה, חנמאל, and שלום. רבי יהודה says: חולדה הנביאה was also a descendant of רחב הזונה. It is written here 'son of תקוה', and it is written there 'this cord (תקות) of scarlet thread'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עינא סבא challenges רב נחמן from a ברייתא. רבי יהודה says there that חולדה descended from רחב, not from יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list of eight prophets sets up the challenge. The key line is רבי יהודה's: חולדה's family line has 'בן תקוה', and רחב was saved by tying a 'תקות חוט השני' (scarlet cord). If חולדה comes from רחב, how can רב נחמן say she comes from יהושע? The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (from a תנאי source such as a ברייתא)
רחב the harlot (or innkeeper) of יריחו, who hid the spies and later joined the Jewish people
The cord of scarlet thread that רחב hung in her window to be saved

steps.confusionAlert: Only the last part of the ברייתא (רבי יהודה's addition about חולדה) is the actual challenge. The list of eight prophets is background showing that רחב had prophetic descendants.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the question of how חולדה could descend from both יהושע and רחב, which the גמרא will resolve next.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב עֵינָא סָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Eina the Elder challenged Rav Nachman:
Eight prophets, who were also Kohanim,
came from Rachav the harlot,
and these are they: Neriah, Baruch,
and Seraiah, Machseyah, Yirmiyah,
Chilkiyah, Chanamel, and Shalum.
Rabbi Yehudah says:
Chuldah the prophetess as well

phrases.aramaic: מִבְּנֵי בָנֶיהָ שֶׁל רָחָב הַזּוֹנָה הָיְתָה.
phrases.english: was one of the descendants of Rachav the harlot.
It is written here: 'son of Tikvah',
and it is written there:
'this cord (tikvas) of scarlet thread'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב עֵינָא סָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's claim that חולדה descended from יהושע.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's statement that חולדה descended from יהושע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא (רבי יהודה) traces חולדה to רחב through the word-link תקוה / תקות, which seems to contradict tracing her to יהושע.

steps.title: Both statements are true: רחב married יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן resolves the contradiction by joining both statements. רחב converted and married יהושע, so חולדה descends from both of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: "עינא סבא" (and some say he called him "blackened pot"), the answer comes from combining what I said and what you said. רחב converted, and יהושע married her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the challenge from step 29. He says there is no contradiction, because both statements fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said חולדה came from רחב, and רב נחמן said she came from יהושע. If רחב converted and married יהושע, their children came from both of them. So the two family lines are really one line, and both statements are correct.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Blackened pot.' An affectionate nickname for a scholar whose face became dark from hard Torah study.
'From me and from you the teaching is completed.' Both of our statements together give the full answer.

steps.confusionAlert: "פַּתְיָא אוּכָּמָא" is not an insult. It is a compliment. It refers to a scholar who worked so hard at learning that his face became 'blackened' like a pot.

phrases.english: He (Rav Nachman) said to him: Eina the Elder,
and some say he said: Blackened pot,
phrases.notes: A nickname of respect for a hardworking scholar.

phrases.english: from me and from you the teaching will be completed:
that she (Rachav) converted, and Yehoshua married her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised by רב עינא סבא in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: both family lines merge into one through a marriage.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Coming from יהושע and coming from רחב seemed to be two different family lines that could not both be true.
steps.terutzMaskana: רחב converted and married יהושע, so חולדה descends from both of them.

steps.title: Did יהושע have any descendants?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. A פסוק in דברי הימים lists יהושע as the last name in his family line, which suggests he had no children.
steps.simpleTranslation: But did יהושע have any descendants? It is written: "נון his son, יהושע his son," and the list stops there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's answer. It asks how חולדה could descend from יהושע if he seems to have had no children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The family list in דברי הימים ends with יהושע and names no son after him. That suggests יהושע had no children. If so, nobody could descend from him, and the answer in step 30 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But isn't it written?' Introduces a פסוק that contradicts the claim.
'נון his son, יהושע his son' (דברי הימים א ז:כז). The family list ends at יהושע.

phrases.english: But did Yehoshua have any offspring?
But isn't it written: "Nun his son, Yehoshua his son"!
phrases.notes: The list stops at יהושע, which implies he had no son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 30 by questioning whether יהושע had any descendants.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חולדה descends from יהושע (steps 28 and 30).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The family list in דברי הימים ends at יהושע. That implies he had no children, so no one could descend from him.

steps.title: יהושע had daughters, not sons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that יהושע had no sons, which is why the list stops at him. He did have daughters, and חולדה descends from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not have sons, but he did have daughters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 31. The פסוק only shows that יהושע had no sons. He did have daughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A family list like this follows the male line, so the list ends when there are no sons. That does not mean יהושע had no children at all. His daughters continued his family, so חולדה can be a descendant of יהושע and רחב.
steps.whatToRemember: חולדה descends from both יהושע and רחב. רחב converted and married יהושע, and their line continued through daughters. That is why the פסוק lists no son after יהושע.

phrases.english: Sons he did not have,
daughters he did have.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנֵי לָא הֲווֹ לֵיהּ, בְּנָתָא הֲווֹ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31 and keeps the answer of step 30 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the inference: the פסוק only shows there were no sons, not that there were no children at all.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the list ends at יהושע, it seemed he had no descendants at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: יהושע had daughters, so his family line, including חולדה, continued through them.
